chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Habbar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who recites one Surah in the two Rak'ahs of the obligatory prayer while he is proficient in others; if he does so, what is upon him? He said: 'If he is proficient in others, he should not do it; and if he is not proficient in others, there is no harm.'

key_terms.فَمَا عَلَيْهِ: what is upon him (i.e., what is the ruling/consequence)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting the same Surah in both Rak'ahs of an obligatory prayer if one knows other Surahs?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the distinction between the obligatory minimum and the recommended excellence (Ihsan) in prayer recitation. It establishes that while repeating a single Surah is legally valid for those lacking proficiency, the preferred Sunnah is to vary the recitation to demonstrate greater devotion and mastery of the Quran.
